entities.summary:
The American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) in New York City is one of the world's largest natural history museums, founded in 1869, with 45 permanent exhibition halls, over 33 million specimens, and 5 million annual visitors. Its collections cover biodiversity, anthropology, astronomy, geology, and paleontology, and it has produced over 1,000 scientific publications annually through its research departments.

The museum was founded by Theodore Roosevelt Sr. (father of President Theodore Roosevelt) and other prominent New Yorkers, and the central Theodore Roosevelt Memorial Hall with its equestrian statue outside became a contested symbol of colonial-era natural history museums — the statue was removed in 2022 following criticism of its racial symbolism depicting Roosevelt with an African and a Native American flanking him.

The museum's collections are foundational to modern science: its meteorite collection is the world's largest; the Rose Center for Earth and Space's Hayden Planetarium has presented cutting-edge cosmology since 1935; Margaret Mead's anthropological work on Pacific cultures was conducted through the museum. The dinosaur halls, including the 94-foot Titanosaur (discovered 2014), are among the world's most complete. The museum was the unlikely setting for the comedy film Night at the Museum (2006), which drove a 20% increase in youth visitors.
